section_summary.extract_value: This section reports a path analysis examining relationships among social safeness, body appreciation, inflexible eating, and eating-disorder psychopathology (EDE-Q). It describes a fully saturated model that was trimmed to remove two nonsignificant paths, then presents coefficients and indirect effects showing that social safeness influences EDE-Q indirectly via body appreciation and inflexible eating. The section does not label any study number (e.g., 'Study 1') and provides no participant/sample demographic or methodological details.
section_summary.evidence_source: "The readjusted model revealed that all path coefficients were statistically significant... Results indicated that social safeness accounted for 25% of body appreciation... social safeness presented an indirect effect on EDE-Q, of −0.17 (95% CI −0.24 to −0.11), mediated by body appreciation and inflexible eating."

section_summary.extract_value: The section reports a path analysis in which an initial saturated model (20 parameters) was trimmed by removing two nonsignificant paths; the final model demonstrated excellent fit (χ2(2)=2.99, p=0.87; CFI=1.00; TLI=1.02; RMSEA=0.00). Results indicate social safeness has a positive direct effect on body appreciation and indirect effects on inflexible eating and eating-disorder psychopathology (EDE-Q) mediated via body appreciation and inflexible eating. The section references Fig. 1 for the summarized mediation pathways.
